text: I dislike the way some of the nurses work. The hospital, Prungjit, is making my mental health worse. I went for treatment as scheduled by the doctor, not intending to see them, but when I did, they made a displeased face. Couldn't they just not look at me? What was the point of staring at me?

This is a large specialized hospital located in the city. Most of its patients have mental health issues. Medical staff need a considerable amount of patience and calmness in providing care. I offer my encouragement.

The male employee who answered the phone was extremely rude, seemingly answering casually. He didn't understand anything I asked.

The Facebook page was full of news about the director going to meetings outside, taking photos, and no activities. He didn't directly care about the hospital's patients. He only held meetings and nothing about the quality of life of the hospital's patients.

The condition of the general ward was like a prison. It was old and rundown, like it was built during World War II. It was dirty, there was no privacy, no green space. All day, they just ate and slept, confiscated their phones, and the TV was full of annoying advertisements.

I moved to a private room, which was expensive, but the condition was no different from the general room. It got a little better. As the days went by, it became very boring. I couldn't contact the outside world. I felt even more depressed and depressed.

I took my boyfriend for treatment and he stayed there for two weeks. The doctors, nurses, and the entire staff in the building took very good care of me. They were both patients and people who were coming for drug addiction treatment. I recommend coming here. The treatment costs are not expensive.
In any hospital, there are always one or two people who talk a lot. Here, there's this old lady with glasses, sitting at desk 4 on October 14th, 2013 at 2:29 PM. I wish she'd read this.
In addition to mental health counseling, they also have a dental department. The doctor is kind, and the assistants and staff provide excellent guidance and service.

Just calling to inquire and being connected to an operator was already a bad experience. The first call was cut off.
The second call was cut off too. The third person who answered spoke like they …

I called to inquire about receiving medication by mail because the patient lives in a high-risk area (Bangkok) and cannot attend appointments for medication due to fear of contracting COVID-19 during travel. The call was connected to the pharmacy, where a male employee stated that I should contact a new hospital and start treatment there (I felt abandoned and told to fend for myself). They don't offer mail-order medication, even though the patient has been receiving continuous treatment for 5 years and requires ongoing medication for this condition. This demonstrates the hospital's poor management. I urge the management and staff to improve their operations and personnel. Don't be so apathetic. Please be mindful of the government budget. #From someone who pays your bills

On November 5th, 2019 (today), I brought a relative from Phitsanulok to see a doctor. We traveled since 4 AM. Upon entering the hospital, I was very impressed with all the staff.

- First, the security guard politely helped us find parking.

Once we found a parking spot, two people quickly came to help direct us, and another person in civilian clothes (probably a member of the public) also helped.
They were all very cheerful and provided excellent service. I even felt guilty for not buying them coffee because I was busy checking on my patient.

1. The first point, the man in the yellow uniform at the registration point, was very helpful and attentive.

2. The point where we filled out the medical history information, was also very helpful. He urged us to fill it out quickly because he was worried we wouldn't make it in time for the morning queue. He did his best, and we managed to get in on time for the afternoon queue (very impressed, worth the wait).
3. The new patient registration point was good.
4. The screening point, queue B, number 2, was very polite to everyone.
5. The man (or woman) at the social welfare office provided excellent service, was very helpful and polite.
6. The doctor at the social welfare office was very polite and gave excellent advice.
7. Dr. Wachana, who examined me in room 4, gave excellent advice. I forgot my medical certificate after the examination and went back to request it, but he was still very helpful and not annoyed at all.
8. The finance department provided good service and the staff were polite.
9. The pharmacy counter (front counter 8, male staff member) provided excellent service and advice. After receiving my medication, I forgot something and went back to have the medication description written down. He wrote it for me and gave helpful advice with a smile.
10. The referral room for patients returning to their place of residence provided excellent advice and service.

Everything was completed with a smile on everyone's faces. The service was incredibly impressive. Everyone was chatting amongst themselves. It would be wonderful if all hospital staff were like this. Everyone was tired, but they had a great spirit and excellent ethics.

Usually, you only see this in luxurious, expensive hospitals in Bangkok, but even those aren't always good in every department.

The only places with excellent service in every department are 5-star hotels.

But this hospital made me and my companion feel better than we would at a luxury hotel. There was more than just smiles and service; there was genuine sincerity and a feeling of genuine kindness from within. Thank you to everyone, and thank you to the director for selecting such good staff to serve the public. I will remember this day and continue to support everyone.

Oh... and thank you to the relative of the patient I was with as well, while I was looking for the restroom. They were also very helpful, even walking me to the restroom.

Driving there and back was tiring, but I was incredibly impressed. It's beyond words.

Somkiat Chainbarameetham

My experience at a terrible psychiatric hospital was awful. Even people with sound judgment could be admitted if they were accused of being addicted to games, when in reality, they just had to share rooms with other patients with more severe conditions, especially those with mental illnesses and substance abuse. I was one of those who had to spend months there without any training or education whatsoever. All I did was sit around, eat, watch TV, and shower and sleep, without any real treatment.

The staff did a great job, especially the psychologist. The hospital atmosphere was relaxing. The only problem was that one doctor seemed unwilling to treat patients, his tone and words suggesting he was sitting with his arms crossed while …

I called to inquire about hospital services, specifically regarding social security insurance at a certain hospital. However, I had heard that Suanprung Hospital also offers good treatment and medication, so I contacted them.

But the male staff member who answered the phone was very impolite. He said, "You can't just come in for service out of the blue." I was only calling to inquire. If that's such a rude first impression, then I might as well not be served.

(I'm speechless.)

I'd like to express my deepest gratitude to the doctors, nurses, and all the staff for the excellent care my wife received. Her condition has improved significantly.
I'd like to offer my support to all the patients and their families, as they stay strong and overcome this critical time in their lives.
Thank you.

The service was excellent, and the doctor, Dr. Kritanat, was incredibly kind. He gave wonderful advice. My son has a brain problem; he had seizures at 4 months old, so he's a special needs child. He also has epilepsy. He's from Kanchanaburi but lives in Chiang Mai. The doctor adjusted my son's medication, and his condition has improved, but it's still not stable. Thank you so much to the doctor and all the staff.

text:
The hospital's patient ID cards are shoddy and shoddy. They're thin, colored paper with holes cut out. They should improve and improve. They even have a note saying not to lose them, but they're so careless. If they were lost, I wouldn't be surprised. It's a regional hospital, and medications aren't free and can't be reimbursed. They should improve and improve. Honestly, the loyalty cards from bubble tea shops are better.
The doctors' research on the disease isn't accurate. In some cases, they assume everyone is mentally ill, when that's not the case. In some cases, they need to refer them to a neurologist to be properly treated. The medication is so strong that it depresses the nervous system, making you feel dizzy and hungover all the time. The first 3-4 days are especially frustrating. You should probably take time off work.

I'm inquiring about my appointment slip because I lost it. I don't know the date and time, but when I called, they told me to hold the line, and the conversation was really unclear. I didn't even get to talk to the doctor; they just took my medical history from another hospital and prescribed medication. 😌 …

The staff member who answered the phone was impolite. We were calling to ask basic questions about what to do if we went in, because we'd never been there before. We weren't asking for free treatment, so we were just asking for general information. The tone of voice clearly revealed the kind of society and family background they came from.

I came just to get a certificate. I've been using the service since 9:00 AM. I had to wait in line for a very long time. The doctor took a long time to take my medical history. Plus, there was a 2-hour lunch break. I took a break from 11:30 …

How long does it take to process a referral slip? I waited for over two hours and still wasn't called. It was past 4 PM, a new shift of staff came, and there were no more patients, but I still hadn't received it. I had to go home and come back another day. They should have told me it was taking so long so I could have left the request and come back the next day.

The management system is very poor. I wonder if some of the people in this hospital have a habit of stealing? They have a bad habit of taking other people's things that aren't their own! It's no wonder why the society in the hospital is so bad.

The staff, doctors, and nurses provided excellent medical advice and services. Everyone was very kind, and the service was as good as what you would get at a private hospital. The COVID vaccine service was fast and very convenient. I was very impressed.

If you are a good person, you can recover and work like everyone else.
If you are not a good person, you have to go back in again.
I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the hospital
and all the doctors
for taking such good care of all the patients.

The male operator was very rude. He hung up before I could finish asking. Even though the hospital staff and doctors were working hard, some of the staff members were ruining the hospital's image. This is not okay.
